drug-prices.name: Medicine prices
drug-prices.line: I worry I won't be able to afford the medicine I need.

sources.passage: 59% of the public now say they are at least somewhat worried about being able to afford prescription drugs
This includes about one in five (22%) who are “very worried” about affording prescription drug costs.

drug-prices.prevalence: 59% of U.S. adults are at least somewhat worried about affording prescription drugs, and 22% are very worried (KFF).

short-staffed-care.name: Not enough doctors
short-staffed-care.line: I see clinics and hospitals without enough doctors and nurses.

sources.passage: 30 - Country Average 47% 43% 33% 23% 23% 20% 19% 17% 8% 8% 7% 2% Access to treatment/ long waiting times Not enough staff Cost of accessing treatment Ageing population Bureaucracy Lack of investment in preventative health Lack of investment Poor quality treatment Poor safety Lack of choice Low standards of cleanliness Other

short-staffed-care.prevalence: Across 30 countries, 43% name not enough staff as one of the biggest problems facing their healthcare system (Ipsos).

hospital-closing.name: Hospital closures
hospital-closing.line: The hospital near me closed or cut services, so care is farther away.

sources.passage: This year's analysis reveals that 417 rural hospitals are vulnerable to closure.
206 rural hospitals have either closed or converted to models that exclude inpatient care

leads: Founder pool: getting healthcare requires more travel time than I can comfortably manage
hospital-closing.prevalence: 417 U.S. rural hospitals are vulnerable to closure, and 206 have closed or stopped inpatient care (Chartis).

no-health-insurance.name: No insurance
no-health-insurance.line: I don't have health insurance, or I'm about to lose it.

sources.passage: In 2025, 26.7 million people (7.9 percent) were uninsured for the entire year

no-health-insurance.prevalence: 26.7 million people in the U.S. (7.9 percent) had no health insurance for all of 2025 (Census Bureau).

obesity.name: Obesity
obesity.line: I see more people struggling with their weight and the illnesses that come with it.

sources.passage: 30 - Country Average 45% 41% 31% 25% 23% 19% 16% 16% 13% 8% 6% 4% 4% 2% Mental Health Cancer Stress Obesity Drug abuse Diabetes Alcohol abuse Heart Disease Smoking Dementia Coronavirus/COVID - 19 Sexually transmitted diseases (STD) Hospital superbugs Other
The prevalence of obesity among U.S. adults 20 and over was 41.9% during 2017–March 2020.

obesity.prevalence: Across 30 countries, 25% name obesity as one of the biggest health problems (Ipsos); 41.9% of U.S. adults had obesity in 2017–March 2020 (CDC).

chronic-disease.name: Chronic disease
chronic-disease.line: I see cancer, heart disease and diabetes taking more people I know.

sources.passage: 30 - Country Average 45% 41% 31% 25% 23% 19% 16% 16% 13% 8% 6% 4% 4% 2% Mental Health Cancer Stress Obesity Drug abuse Diabetes Alcohol abuse Heart Disease Smoking Dementia Coronavirus/COVID - 19 Sexually transmitted diseases (STD) Hospital superbugs Other
The world's biggest killer is ischaemic heart disease, responsible for 16% of the world's total deaths.
claiming 2.0 million lives, more than double the deaths in 2000

chronic-disease.prevalence: Across 30 countries, 41% name cancer, 19% diabetes and 16% heart disease among the biggest health problems (Ipsos). Ischaemic heart disease causes 16% of deaths worldwide (WHO).

pandemics.name: Pandemics
pandemics.line: I worry about the next pandemic or a disease our medicines can't stop.

sources.passage: In 2023 it claimed 2.7 million lives, returning back up to its 2019 pre-pandemic level.

30 - Country Average 45% 41% 31% 25% 23% 19% 16% 16% 13% 8% 6% 4% 4% 2% Mental Health Cancer Stress Obesity Drug abuse Diabetes Alcohol abuse Heart Disease Smoking Dementia Coronavirus/COVID - 19 Sexually transmitted diseases (STD) Hospital superbugs Other

pandemics.prevalence: Lower respiratory infections killed 2.7 million people in 2023 (WHO); across 30 countries, 6% still name COVID-19 among the biggest health problems (Ipsos).

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.line: I'm watching dementia take away people I love.

sources.passage: Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia ranked as the fifth leading cause of death, killing 2.1 million people.

dementia.prevalence: Alzheimer's disease and other dementias killed 2.1 million people worldwide, the fifth leading cause of death (WHO); across 30 countries, 8% name dementia among the biggest health problems (Ipsos).

care-quality.name: Poor care
care-quality.line: I don't trust the care I get to be good or safe.

sources.passage: 30 - Country Average 47% 43% 33% 23% 23% 20% 19% 17% 8% 8% 7% 2% Access to treatment/ long waiting times Not enough staff Cost of accessing treatment Ageing population Bureaucracy Lack of investment in preventative health Lack of investment Poor quality treatment Poor safety Lack of choice Low standards of cleanliness Other

pregnancy-care.name: Pregnancy care
pregnancy-care.line: I worry about getting safe care through pregnancy and birth.

sources.passage: In 2024, 649 women died of maternal causes in the United States, compared with 669 in 2023
The maternal mortality rate for 2024, 17.9 deaths per 100,000 live births
Between 2011 and 2024, 331 rural hospitals stopped offering OB services.

pregnancy-care.prevalence: 649 women died of maternal causes in the U.S. in 2024, 17.9 per 100,000 live births (CDC); 331 rural hospitals stopped offering obstetrics between 2011 and 2024 (Chartis).

medicine-shortages.name: Medicine shortages
medicine-shortages.line: I can't get a medicine I rely on because it's out of stock.
leads: Founder pool: a medication I rely on is difficult or impossible to obtain
